2027-11-01.name: Daily #396
hints: The beam already passes close to the seed. One mass beside it can pull it across.
The marked sphere holds the mass, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam.
A medium mass one and a half shadow-widths from the beam, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam, turns it onto the seed.
2027-11-01.teach: Light passing a mass bends toward it, twice as much as Newton predicted.

2027-11-02.name: Daily #397
hints: After a bend the light runs straight again. Make that new line pass through every seed.
The marked sphere holds the mass, about a third of the way along the star's beam.
A medium mass one and a half shadow-widths from the beam, about a third of the way along the star's beam, turns it through every seed.
2027-11-02.teach: After a bend light runs straight again: one bend can line up two seeds.

2027-11-03.name: Daily #398
hints: No single bend reaches every seed: the beam must turn one way, then back the other.
The marked sphere holds the first mass, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam.

A medium mass one and a half shadow-widths from the beam, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam, turns it toward the second mass. Then a medium mass a shadow-width from the new beam, before the first seed, turns it back through every seed.
2027-11-03.teach: One mass bends light one way only; an S-shaped path needs two.

2027-11-04.name: Daily #399
hints: A mass only pulls the beam toward itself. These seeds need a turn one way, then a turn back.
The marked sphere holds the first mass, close to the star.

A heavy mass a shadow-width from the beam, close to the star, turns it toward the second mass. Then a heavy mass a shadow-width from the new beam, before the first seed, turns it back through every seed.
2027-11-04.teach: Each mass pulls light toward itself, so turning one way and then back takes two.

2027-11-05.name: Daily #400
hints: No single bend reaches every seed: the beam must turn one way, then back the other. The heavy mass makes the sharper turn.
The marked sphere holds the first mass, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam.

A light mass one and a half shadow-widths from the beam, about a quarter of the way along the star's beam, turns it toward the second mass. Then a heavy mass a shadow-width from the new beam, before the first seed, turns it back through every seed.
2027-11-05.teach: The bend grows with the mass: twice the mass, twice the turn at the same distance.
